record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: Consider the process of randomly choosing a Young diagram of sizen. If we letn→ ∞and scale the diagram down by √nin both dimensions, the average of the diagrams converges to a limit shape; points within the shape have probability 1 of being in the random diagram and points outside the shape have probability 0. Surprisingly, the same limit shape results under three distributions on the set of diagrams: uniform (weight 1), uniform on Young tableaux (weightf λ, the number of tableaux of shapeλ), and the Plancherel measure (weightf 2 λ). Perform the parallel analysis on shifted Young diagrams, the set of partitions into distinct parts. Since the RSK algorithm for shifted diagrams has a weighting (c λ = 2|λ|−ℓ(λ)), there are now six plausible distributions: 1,g λ,g 2 λ, cλ,g λcλ, andg 2 λcλ, whereg λ is the number of shifted Young tableaux (without coloring) of shapeλ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{D}_n$ denote the set of strict partitions of $n$, i.e., partitions $\lambda = (\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots > \lambda_{\ell(\lambda)} > 0)$ of $n$ into distinct positive parts; identify each such partition with its shifted Young diagram (the diagram with $\lambda_i$ cells in row $i$, where row $i$ is shifted $i-1$ units to the right). For $\lambda \in \mathcal{D}_n$, let:
- $g^\lambda$ be the number of standard shifted Young tableaux of shape $\lambda$ (uncolored),
- $c_\lambda = 2^{|\lambda|-\ell(\lambda)}$, where $|\lambda|=n$ and $\ell(\lambda)$ is the number of parts of $\lambda$.

For each weight function $w \in \{1,\ g^\lambda,\ (g^\lambda)^2,\ c_\lambda,\ g^\lambda c_\lambda,\ (g^\lambda)^2 c_\lambda\}$, define the probability measure on $\mathcal{D}_n$ by $\mathbb{P}^{(w)}_n(\lambda) = w(\lambda) / Z^{(w)}_n$, where $Z^{(w)}_n = \sum_{\mu \in \mathcal{D}_n} w(\mu)$.

Embed each shifted diagram $\lambda$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ as the union of unit cells, and rescale by the factor $1/\sqrt{n}$ in both coordinate directions, obtaining a region $\widetilde{\lambda}_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$.

For each of the six measures, determine whether there exists a deterministic limit shape $\Omega^{(w)} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, as $n \to \infty$, the rescaled random shifted diagram $\widetilde{\lambda}_n$ (with $\lambda$ drawn from $\mathbb{P}^{(w)}_n$) converges in probability to $\Omega^{(w)}$ in the sense that for every point in the interior of $\Omega^{(w)}$ the probability of belonging to $\widetilde{\lambda}_n$ tends to $1$ and for every point outside $\Omega^{(w)}$ this probability tends to $0$. Identify each limit shape $\Omega^{(w)}$ explicitly, and determine which of the six measures yield the same limit shape (in particular, whether — analogously to the unshifted case where the weights $1$, $f^\lambda$, and $(f^\lambda)^2$ all give the same limit shape — some or all of the six shifted measures coincide).
artifact.category_tag: Limit shapes of random shifted Young diagrams
artifact.status_search_result: Limit shapes are individually known for several of the six measures: for the uniform measure on strict partitions (weight 1), the limit shape was established by Vershik (building on Erdős–Lehner and Szalay–Turán); for the shifted Plancherel measure (weight $(g^\lambda)^2 c_\lambda /n!$), a limit shape was obtained by Borodin and others, and is studied e.g. by Matsumoto and in Petrov's work on random strict partitions and random shifted tableaux. However, a unified comparative analysis showing whether all six listed weightings yield the same (or different) limit shape does not appear to have been carried out in the literature, so the question as posed is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Random strict partitions and random shifted tableaux
status_evidence.snippet: Limit shape results for random shifted Young diagrams under Plancherel-type measures on strict partitions.
status_evidence.claim: Limit shape under shifted Plancherel measure (weight $(g^\lambda)^2 c_\lambda$) is known.

status_evidence.title: Limit Shape of Minimal Difference Partitions and Fractional Statistics
status_evidence.snippet: For strict partitions (distinct parts), the limit shape was implicitly contained in Erdős–Lehner and obtained rigorously by Vershik using Szalay–Turán estimates.
status_evidence.claim: Limit shape for uniform measure on strict partitions (weight 1) is established.

status_evidence.title: Plancherel measures on strict partitions: Polynomiality
status_evidence.snippet: Plancherel measure on strict partitions defined via $2^{n-\ell(\xi)}(g^\xi)^2/n!$.
status_evidence.claim: The shifted Plancherel measure corresponds to weight $(g^\lambda)^2 c_\lambda$ in the problem.
